name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1 June 2026 and completed my full 60-day notice period till my last working day on 31 July 2026. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My June salary was delayed, and my July salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
Core Legal Standing: You have a valid civil employment claim for your unpaid wages and dues, governed by the Code on Wages, 2019.
Key Statutory Rule: Under Section 17(2), wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within two working days of their last working day.
Immediate Takeaway: Send a formal written demand email to your employer citing Section 17(2) and approach the competent labour authority for recovery if they fail to pay.

As an ex-employee who successfully completed your resignation and notice period ending on 31 July 2026, you possess a clear right under the Code on Wages, 2019 to receive your final wages within two working days of your departure. Because your last working day was 31 July 2026 (which is after the 21 November 2025 commencement date of the Code on Wages, 2019), Section 17(2) fully applies to your wage dues. 

Please note that non-payment of salary is strictly a civil employment dispute, not a criminal matter, so filing a criminal police complaint or FIR for a salary delay is legally improper. Regarding your relieving letter and experience certificate, please remember that no fixed legal deadline is stated in the law for these documents; you should check your employment contract and company policy, or consult a lawyer. For your wage claims, the District LegalServices Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Helpline 15100 is available to provide free legal aid and guidance only, and is not an adjudicating forum for proceedings against your employer.

governing_laws.relevance: Mandates that the wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within two working days of their resignation or last working day.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: Since this involves formal employment claims, recovery of withheld dues, and potential complications regarding relieving letters, consulting a licensed advocate or seeking guidance from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA Helpline 15100) is strongly recommended.

legal_notice_draft:
### LEGAL NOTICE DRAFT – REVIEW BEFORE SENDING

**FROM:** 
[Your Name] 
[Your Address] 
Phone: [Your Phone Number] 
Email: [Your Email Address] 

**DATE:** 09/11/2026

**MODE OF DISPATCH:** Speed Post with Acknowledgement Due (AD) / Registered Email

**TO:** 
The Management / Human Resources Department 
IT Consultancy Firm 
Cyber City, Gurugram 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE FOR NON-PAYMENT OF FINAL SALARY, LEAVE ENCASHMENT, AND WITHHOLDING OF RELIEVING DOCUMENTS**

Dear Sir/Madam,

I, **[Your Name]**, residing at **[Your Address]**, do hereby serve you with this formal legal demand notice on my own behalf, stating and submitting as under:

1. That I was employed with your IT consultancy firm as a frontend developer, having rendered dedicated services for a period of 18 months prior to July 2026 under the terms of my appointment letter.

2. That on 1 June 2026, I formally submitted my resignation, duly initiating and serving my 60-day notice period as per company policy.

3. That my last working day successfully concluded on 31 July 2026, upon the completion of my notice period. On the said date, I completed the complete asset handover and received the official asset clearance certificate from the IT department, alongside a signed clearance form.

4. That despite my full and final discharge of duties, asset handover, and clearance, you have unlawfully withheld my legitimate statutory and contractual dues amounting to **Rs. 1,65,000**, which specifically includes my unpaid salary for the month of June 2026, unpaid salary for the month of July 2026, and 15 days of encashable leave.

5. That even by 50 days post-last working day (around late September 2026), my pending dues remain completely unpaid, and HR has unjustifiably cited internal client payment delays while simultaneously withholding my essential relieving letter and experience certificate.

6. That my rightful claim is governed by the **Code on Wages, 2019**. Specifically, under **Section 17(2)** of the said Code, the wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within two working days of their last working day. As my last working day was 31 July 2026 (which is subsequent to the commencement date of the Code on Wages, 2019), Section 17(2) fully applies to my wage dues, and your failure to clear these payments within the statutory window constitutes a clear violation of law.

7. That while I note no fixed legal deadline is stated in the law for the issuance of relieving letters and experience certificates (the terms for which should be checked against employment contracts and company policies), withholding these documents indefinitely after complete clearance and asset handover causes severe prejudice to my career and professional standing.

8. That I have maintained email communications with HR regarding these salary delays, but no constructive resolution has been provided to date.

---

### **DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION**

I hereby call upon you to clear my total outstanding dues amounting to **Rs. 1,65,000** and issue my formal relieving letter and experience certificate within a suggested **15-day period** (customary pre-litigation practice) from the date of receipt of this notice. 

Please remit the aforementioned amount directly to my bank account on record, details of which are available with your finance department, and confirm the same in writing.

### **WARNING**

In the event of your failure to settle my dues and release my relieving documents within the suggested 15-day rectification window, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal proceedings by approaching the competent labour authority (confirm locally) for the recovery of my wages, along with seeking further appropriate legal remedies available to me under law, entirely at your risk as to costs and consequences.

For guidance and free legal aid regarding my rights, I may also reach out to the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: **15100**.

---

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name] 

---

**ANNEXURE INVENTORY (Copies Enclosed/Referenced):**
1. Appointment Letter
2. Resignation Acceptance Email
3. Signed Clearance Form
4. Asset Clearance Certificate from IT Department
5. Email Communications with HR Regarding Salary Delays

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre, District Labor Commissioner ko kyun beech mein la rahe ho? Company policy clear hai—pehle internal clearance aur client feedback review hoga, uske baad hi full and final settlement process hota hai. Agreement padha tha na joining ke waqt? 90 days ka buffer period hota hai accounting verification ke liye. Aur waise bhi, tumhara notice period aur asset handover ka kuch discrepancy hai accounts team ke paas. Thoda wait karo, khud call aa jayega HR se!

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You firmly demanded your pending dues and relieving letter while setting a clear 3-day deadline, and highlighted how withholding documents impacts your livelihood.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Avoid citing outside labor acts not in our database. Instead, focus strictly on the Code on Wages, 2019 provisions regarding timely wage payment upon termination or resignation.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, my earned wages for June and July along with leave encashment must be paid immediately upon exit, and holding my relieving documents is illegal.
